name: Mini Cooper S (works rally)
hook: Three of these finished first, second and third at Monte Carlo in 1966, and all three were thrown out over their headlight bulbs.
story: Monte Carlo, January 1966. Three works Minis come down off the mountain first, second and third. Timo Mäkinen, Rauno Aaltonen, Paddy Hopkirk — the three Musketeers, driving a 1,275 cc saloon that has just beaten cars with twice the engine. Then the scrutineers start on the lights. Hours later the verdict lands. The Minis are running single-filament quartz-iodine headlamp bulbs, and the officials rule that the dipping beam no longer meets the letter of the regulations. All three are excluded. So is the Lotus Cortina that finished fourth. The win passes down to Pauli Toivonen, fifth on the road in a Citroën DS. The cars had already passed scrutineering before the start. Toivonen took the trophy, called it hollow, and said he would never drive for Citroën again. The British press called it robbery. BMC came back the next January and Aaltonen won outright, with nothing left to argue about. The 1966 result still stands in the record books. Almost nobody quotes it.
description: The Mini Cooper S was a tuned version of Alec Issigonis's 1959 Mini, developed with the racing constructor John Cooper. The 1275 S carried a 1,275 cc A-series four, twin carburettors and front disc brakes in a car barely three metres long. BMC's competition department at Abingdon turned it into a rally car. It won the Monte Carlo Rally in 1964, 1965 and 1967, out-driving far bigger machinery on narrow, snow-covered mountain roads.
